newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-PETER KIRSTEN SET FOR FIRST-CLASS FAREWELL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PETER KIRSTEN SET FOR FIRST-CLASS FAREWELL.

text.p: Veteran South African batsman Peter Kirsten marks his farewell from first-class cricket in the three-day game between Border and Australia starting on Friday and, at 41, believes the timing is right.

"Obviously to play against Australia is a grand occasion which brings out the best in you - or maybe even the worst of you! But I'm ready for it, I'm very prepared and I believe that now is the right time for me to bow out of cricket," Kirsten said on Thursday.

In a first-class career spanning 25 years and embracing glittering achievements with Western Province, Border, Sussex and Derbyshire as well as 12 tests, Kirsten will be remembered as a gifted batsman of subtle touch, nimble footwork and great courage.
Kirsten's last seven years have been with emerging cricket province Border where he has been instrumental in their growing success.

"I've really enjoyed being able to help them to become a respectable and competitive province. And, at a personal level, I will always cherish memories of my highest score at first-class level...271 against Northern Transvaal in 1994," Kirsten said.

That innings surpassed his previous highest score of 228 for Derbyshire against Somerset in 1981 and saw him become, at the age of 38, the first South African batsman to have scored eight first-class double centuries - only two of which were compiled n South Africa.
Kirsten averages 44.63 and has scored 57 centuries and 107 half-centuries in his first-class career.
